summary: Learn practical prompt engineering for legal, risk and compliance. Build safer prompts, validation checks, and governance templates. Enquire now.
lede: Prompt engineering for legal, risk and compliance gives teams a disciplined way to design prompts, set constraints, and review AI outputs for regulated work. It supports more accurate drafting, source-based validation, red-flag detection, confidentiality controls, and documented decisions that strengthen governance and auditability. This course turns inconsistent prompting habits into a practical system for policy drafting, regulatory summaries, clause analysis, issue spotting, and control narratives. Through hands-on exercises, you will build safer prompts, test outputs against source documents, and create review checklists and AI use logs that support reliable work under real operational constraints.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to use generative AI safely in legal, risk and compliance work, with outputs they can review, defend, and reuse. In-house Counsel managing AI-assisted drafting, review, and escalation decisions. Compliance Officer preparing policy summaries, controls narratives, and monitoring reports. Risk Analyst testing prompt outputs against risk scenarios and issue registers. Legal Operations Manager standardizing prompt workflows and review checkpoints. Contract Manager using prompts for clause extraction and deviation tracking. Privacy Officer checking prompts for sensitive data handling and retention issues. Governance, Risk and Compliance Specialist aligning AI use with control frameworks. Regulatory Affairs Manager summarizing obligations and internal response actions. Internal Auditor assessing prompt logs, validation steps, and evidence trails. Knowledge Management Lead building prompt libraries and approved output templates.
prerequisites: Recommended prerequisites: working familiarity with legal drafting, compliance review, risk assessment, or governance workflows; no coding required. You should be comfortable reading policy documents, control narratives, or regulatory summaries, and you should bring a laptop for hands-on prompt drafting and validation exercises. Prior exposure to generative AI tools is helpful but not required. Advanced concepts such as retrieval-augmented generation and prompt logging are taught at an operational application level, not implementation level.
